title: News Ltd. Planned a 40% Stake in the News of the World After a Pergamon Bid
description_short: A 1968 Guardian report described a planned News Ltd. stake in the News of the World after a Pergamon Press takeover bid.
description_medium: The Guardian reported on October 25, 1968 that News Ltd. planned to take a 40 per cent stake in the News of the World after Pergamon Press, led by Robert Maxwell, made a takeover bid. The report said Rupert Murdoch was to become joint managing director with Sir William Carr. It does not mention Donald Trump or establish a connection to him.
description_long: The Guardian's archive report, published Friday, October 25, 1968, described an arrangement under which News Ltd. was to take a 40 per cent stake in the News of the World after a takeover bid by Pergamon Press, the publishing group headed by Robert Maxwell, was defeated. The report said Rupert Murdoch, then chairman of News Ltd., was to become joint managing director with the newspaper's existing chairman, Sir William Carr. Its wording that the deal was unfolded the previous day places the report of the arrangement on October 24, although the archive item itself is dated October 25. The article describes a British newspaper ownership and management transaction; it does not report a Trump action or relationship. The frozen record's title and synopsis misidentify the newspaper titles and claim a bidding contest involving The Sun, while the accessible Guardian report concerns the News of the World. The linked TrumpFile page was reported in prior research as returning HTTP 202 without readable text. The supplied evidence therefore supports a narrow account of the 1968 transaction but gives no documented reason for placing it in a Trump-focused collection. Keep this copy as an exclusion review draft, not as a Trump-linked entry. The source says the stake and management changes were planned; it does not establish that they were completed.
date_basis: The Guardian report is dated 1968-10-25 and says the deal was unfolded 'yesterday'; event date is inferred as 1968-10-24.

children.title: Trump Orders U.S. Withdrawal from the World Health Organization
children.description_short: A Jan. 20, 2025 order directs steps toward U.S. withdrawal from WHO; it does not say membership ended that day.
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order stating that the United States intended to withdraw from the World Health Organization. It directed officials to pause future U.S. transfers, recall and reassign personnel, identify partners for necessary WHO activities, and cease negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement while withdrawal was in progress. The order does not establish that membership ended on January 20.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order stating that the United States intended to withdraw from the World Health Organization. It directed the Secretary of State and Office of Management and Budget to pause future U.S. funds, support and resources to WHO; recall and reassign government personnel or contractors working with the organization; and identify U.S. and international partners to assume necessary WHO activities. The order also directed the Secretary of State to cease negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement and amendments to the International Health Regulations while withdrawal was in progress. This is an order to pursue withdrawal, not proof that the United States left WHO on January 20. The frozen entry incorrectly said the country withdrew from both WHO and UNESCO that day; the UNESCO action is a separate later claim and is kept in a second internal draft. The order's text does not establish the broader outcome claims in the frozen synopsis, so this card does not state that U.S. departure had already removed the country from disease-surveillance networks or produced quantified public-health harms.

children.title: U.S. UNESCO Withdrawal Decision Reported for July 2025 (Unverified)
children.description_short: Prior research says the U.S. chose to leave UNESCO in July 2025, with departure set for December 2026; the cited page could not be checked.
children.description_medium: According to the supplied packet, UNESCO Director-General Audrey Azoulay announced a U.S. decision to withdraw on July 22, 2025, effective at the end of December 2026. The cited UNESCO page returned an automated human-verification screen and could not be checked. A February 4 White House order required a review of UNESCO membership, not an immediate withdrawal; the July claim remains unverified and this draft is not publication-eligible.
children.description_long: The supplied research packet attributes a July 22, 2025 announcement to UNESCO Director-General Audrey Azoulay and says the United States had decided to withdraw from UNESCO, with departure to take effect at the end of December 2026. Those supplied details correct the frozen entry's January 20 date and distinguish a future withdrawal from a completed exit. The cited UNESCO statement could not be inspected during this review: a direct request returned an automated human-verification screen, while the connected Exa service returned an authorization error and Firecrawl reported that its credits were exhausted. The White House's February 4 order, which was fetched directly, says only that the United States would review its UNESCO membership within 90 days; it does not establish a July withdrawal decision or an enacted departure. This internal draft therefore preserves the supplied chronology for review, labels the central announcement and effective date unverified, and does not state that the United States has already left UNESCO. The original January 20 date is not supported for this UNESCO claim. Publication requires an accessible source excerpt confirming the announcement and timing.

title: Trump Revoked EO 11246 and Changed Federal Contractor DEI Rules
description_short: A Jan. 21 order revoked EO 11246, set a 90-day transition, and limited contractor certification to DEI programs that violate federal law.
description_medium: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump revoked Executive Order 11246, which governed equal-employment requirements for federal contractors. The order allowed contractors to continue under the January 20 regulatory scheme for 90 days during the transition. It directed agencies to require certification that a contractor does not operate DEI programs that violate federal anti-discrimination law; it did not require contractors to eliminate every DEI program.
description_long: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump signed the order “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity.” Section 3 revoked Executive Order 11246, the federal contractor equal-employment order, and allowed contractors to continue complying with the regulatory scheme in effect on January 20 for 90 days. It directed the Labor Department's Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to stop holding contractors responsible for affirmative action and related practices described in the order. The order also required agencies to add contract terms concerning compliance with federal anti-discrimination laws and certification that a contractor does not operate DEI programs that violate those laws. That language is narrower than the frozen entry's claim that all contractor DEI requirements ended immediately or that contractors had to eliminate all DEI programs. The order took effect as an executive directive on January 21, but the 90-day transition means the change was staged. This record describes the order and its text; it makes no claim about court outcomes or documented injuries to a specific contractor, employee, or protected group.
